sources.title: Green Mountain: 'Green Mountain Global Signs Contract with Major Neocloud Operator at LON-East Campus' (press release, 1 September 2026)
sources.publisher: Green Mountain (Green Mountain AS / Green Mountain DC UK Limited)
sources.summary: Green Mountain's release dated 1 September 2026 says it has secured a customer agreement for 14 MW of capacity at its LON-East campus in Romford, East London, under which a neocloud operator (not named) will occupy 'the recently delivered 14 MW of AI-ready capacity'. It describes LON-East as an established 37 MW data-centre campus on major fibre routes, designed for air, liquid and hybrid cooling at rack densities above 100 kW, and states that Green Mountain DC UK acquired the freehold of the eight-acre Romford site in 2026 and has power and planning secured for a further phase of development. Green Mountain UK's managing director is quoted on the agreement.
sources.date_semantics: The page's datePublished (JSON-LD and article:published_time) is 2026-09-01T06:28:58Z and the page itself is dated 1 September 2026; dateModified is 40 seconds later. Used as a 1 September 2026 observation that the 14 MW AI-ready expansion has been delivered (completed). The customer's occupation is stated as future and is not treated as operation of the new capacity; the 37 MW figure is the campus's planned total, not built capacity. The spokesperson's name is not reproduced.

sources.date_semantics: Register record without a publication date; the 21 April 2015 registration date is the permit's original registration, not a status observation. sources.title: Environment Agency Compliance Assessment Report FP3630EU/0598676: site inspection at Romford North Data Centre (Green Mountain DC UK Limited), 29 April 2026, issued 7 May 2026
sources.license: Open Government Licence v3.0 (Environment Agency public register document)
sources.summary: The Environment Agency's general compliance visit to 'Romford North Data Centre' (permit FP3630EU, operator and permit holder Green Mountain DC UK Limited) on 29 April 2026 recorded no breaches. It notes the permit variation EPR/FP3630EU/V002 (received 19 February 2026) for 'Phase VI' with eight new emergency generators with SCR abatement, whose integrated commissioning was at its final stage and not yet handed over to the operator; water and cooling plant for 'the new data halls'; some expansion construction in the back yard; and a planned future 'LON2' expansion with four data halls and twelve engines across King George Close, where a substation is already in place and for which no permit application had yet been made.
sources.date_semantics: Report dated 29 April 2026 (inspection) and issued 7 May 2026, outside the 85-day window. Used only as identity and scope context: it ties Green Mountain DC UK Limited to the Romford North Data Centre permit and shows the new data halls' standby plant in final commissioning before the window. It is not the status observation. Officer and recipient names are redacted in the report.

sources.title: Green Mountain: 'Green Mountain UK acquires freehold of Romford data center campus' (8 June 2026)
sources.publisher: Green Mountain (Green Mountain AS / Green Mountain DC UK Limited)
sources.summary: Green Mountain announced on 8 June 2026 that it had acquired the freehold of its 8-acre data-centre campus in Romford, East London, 'also known as LON-East'. It states that 7 MW has been operational on the site since 2010, that an additional 14 MW 'has been delivered recently', that the campus has a planned total of 37 MW, and that Green Mountain will continue to operate the existing data centre while unlocking the remaining capacity.
sources.date_semantics: Dated 8 June 2026 (datePublished 2026-06-08T10:49:02Z), outside the 85-day window. Used only as identity context: it equates the Romford campus with LON-East and separates the legacy 7 MW operation, the 14 MW expansion and the remaining planned capacity. It is not used as the status observation.

sources.title: Green Mountain: 'Green Mountain breaks ground on new data centre expansion in London' (8 December 2023)
sources.summary: Green Mountain announced in December 2023 that a new 14 MW expansion was under construction at its LON-East campus in Romford, built in two 7 MW phases inside the existing building with over 5,500 sq m of white space (three data halls supporting 7 MW of IT load per phase), after it incorporated Infinity Data Centres into its portfolio in January 2023 and renamed the site LON-East; an additional 16 MW build-to-suit opportunity on an adjacent plot had power and planning permission.
sources.date_semantics: Dated 8 December 2023, far outside the window. Used only to define the scope of the 14 MW expansion (two 7 MW phases inside the existing building) and the site's earlier name; its completion targets are forecasts and are not used.

sources.title: Green Mountain: LON-East data center location page
sources.summary: Green Mountain's LON-East page describes a data centre in Romford, East London, with space in an existing 11,000 m2 building (build year 2009, designed and built to Tier III specifications, dedicated on-site substation, 8.6-acre land footprint) and a planned building of 5,760 m2 (eight 2 MW data halls on 4 acres), 37 MW of secured power capacity, HVO-fuelled automatic standby generators and ISO 9001, 20000, 27001, 45001 and 14001 certification.
sources.date_semantics: Undated operator page; its JSON-LD gives datePublished 18 October 2022 and dateModified 1 September 2026, but no archived copy bounds that modification, and its 'space currently in construction' figure is not used. Used only as identity and facility context; not a status observation.

sources.title: Environment Agency Citizen Space: 'SL0 9JQ, Amazon Data Services UK Limited, EPR/TP3621MM/A001: environmental permit consultation' (opened 24 September 2026, closed 22 October 2026)
sources.license: Open Government Licence v3.0 (Environment Agency consultation page)
sources.summary: The Environment Agency's consultation page, opened 24 September 2026 and closed 22 October 2026, seeks comments on the bespoke environmental permit application EPR/TP3621MM/A001 from Amazon Data Services UK Limited for the 'Ridgeway Data Centre Emergency Back Up Generation Facility', Ridgeway Trading Estate, Iver, Buckinghamshire SL0 9JQ, and lists the application documents (non-technical summary v3 of 10 June 2026, Part A, updated Parts B2 and F1 of 9 July 2026, Part B3, installation-boundary, drainage and emission-point plans, generator data sheets, noise, BAT, site-condition and air-emissions risk assessments). It says the Agency will decide whether to grant or refuse the permit after considering the responses. It is a separate consultation page from the one opened on 13 August 2026 for the same application.
sources.date_semantics: The page states 'Opened 24 Sep 2026' and 'Closed 22 Oct 2026'; 24 September 2026 is used as the date of this regulator record and as an announced observation of the Ridgeway data-centre development, strictly newer than the record's 13 August 2026 advertisement. It is a consultation on an undecided application: no permit decision, planning consent or physical work is implied. The listed application documents are dated before the window and are not separately relied on.
